question: Does a pretrained 12-layer Video Vision Transformer internally distinguish a successful bowling strike from a gutter ball even though both videos receive the same Bowling label, and can attention-versus-MLP activation patching identify a causal action-outcome circuit?

key_findings.claim: The case study finds a growing strike-versus-gutter activation difference in the model's later residual stream, but the evidence is an unnormalized two-video difference rather than a validated semantic outcome variable.
key_findings.evidence: For the one strike/gutter pair, the L2 norm of the CLS-activation delta rises from about 75 at layer 5 to more than 250 at the final layer, an increase exceeding 300%. The authors interpret this as a layer-5-to-11 outcome-signal amplification cascade; no matched controls, random-pair distribution, normalization by activation scale, or repeated videos establish that the increase is specific to success rather than accumulated scene differences.

anchors.section: 4.2 From Failed Experiments to a Clear Signal

key_findings.claim: A layerwise linear probe cannot validate the proposed outcome concept in this experiment because it perfectly separates the two individual videos from layer 0.
key_findings.evidence: Logistic probes trained to distinguish strike from gutter CLS activations report 100% accuracy at every layer. The paper itself labels this a failed 'fingerprint scanner' result: with only two underlying clips, low-level and scene-specific differences already separate the classes before any putative semantic computation.

key_findings.claim: Attention visualizations qualitatively track bowling-relevant regions, but they do not isolate an outcome detector.
key_findings.evidence: Layer-9 head 8 attends to ball-pin interaction patches; layer-10 head 8 follows the ball and pins in the strike clip and the gutter and untouched pins in the failure clip. These are single-example attention overlays without counterfactual localization tests, head ablations, or measurements showing that the attended regions encode success rather than generic bowling content.

key_findings.claim: Zeroing the 10% of spatiotemporal tokens with the largest positive Bowling-logit attribution barely changes the Bowling prediction for either clip.
key_findings.evidence: The intervention zeros 313 patches. The strike Bowling logit falls from 16.9954 to 16.6583, a change of -0.3371, while the gutter Bowling logit falls from 16.5200 to 16.5044, a change of -0.0156; Bowling remains rank 1 in both cases. This supports robustness of the class logit to this particular top-positive-token zero ablation, not the stronger author inference that an outcome circuit operates independently of classification.

key_findings.claim: Whole-block activation patching produces partial recovery of the final strike-minus-gutter delta from both attention and MLP blocks, with MLP recovery larger at layers 4-9 but not at layer 10.
key_findings.evidence: Patching strike activations into the gutter run yields attention/MLP recovery percentages of 54.41/60.17 at layer 4, 50.22/57.49 at layer 5, 43.62/49.11 at layer 6, 40.38/42.55 at layer 7, 37.72/42.10 at layer 8, 44.43/58.66 at layer 9, and 47.61/43.39 at layer 10. Thus the table supports an MLP advantage over layers 4-9, but directly contradicts an unqualified claim that every MLP block is the primary driver: layer-10 attention recovers more than its MLP.

key_findings.claim: No tested attention or MLP block alone recovers the full measured delta, but this does not by itself establish a redundant distributed algorithm.
key_findings.evidence: Every reported block-patching recovery lies between 37.72% and 60.17%. The authors interpret incomplete recovery plus ablation resilience as distributed redundancy; however, whole-block patching in a nonlinear residual network can yield non-additive, path-dependent effects, and no completeness test, double patch, path patch, random patch, or causal-scrubbing baseline distinguishes redundancy from metric and intervention artifacts.

key_findings.claim: The authors explicitly restrict the result to one contrastive pair and one ViViT checkpoint, leaving semantic invariance and generality untested.
key_findings.evidence: The limitations section says scene-specific features such as background texture cannot be ruled out, manual component patching is impractical at scale, and the circuit has not been tested across samples or architectures. Proposed follow-ups include ACDC over a statistically significant Kinetics-400 sample, Integrated Gradients comparisons, and TimeSformer replication.

method.core_idea: Use one minimally contrastive-looking pair of bowling videos that share the same predicted class, locate their internal activation difference across a pretrained ViViT, then intervene on salient tokens and transformer blocks to ask which components can move the gutter representation toward the strike representation.
method.mechanism: The authors run the Hugging Face google/vivit-b-16x2-kinetics400 model on one 10-second strike video and one 10-second gutter video, using stochastic temporal sampling with seed 42. They inspect Direct Logit Attribution, tokenwise target-logit heatmaps, CLS attention, and layerwise logistic probes. They define an outcome delta as act_strike minus act_gutter and use its L2 norm as signal strength. They zero the top 10% DLA-positive spatiotemporal tokens, then separately copy each layer's whole attention-block or MLP-block activation from the strike run into the gutter run. Recovery is a signed ratio of patched-delta norm to the original layer-11 delta norm, and the attention-versus-MLP recovery profile is used to propose an 'attention gathers, MLPs compose' circuit.
assumptions: The two selected videos differ primarily in bowling outcome rather than background, camera, actor, timing, trajectory, lane, lighting, or preprocessing details.
The raw L2 norm of a single activation difference is a meaningful measure of semantic signal strength across layers despite possible differences in representation scale and dimensional geometry.
Copying an entire attention or MLP block activation from one video into the other is a sufficiently localized and on-manifold intervention to assign causal function to that block.

The signed norm-ratio recovery metric meaningfully measures movement along the strike outcome direction even though norm and sign do not quantify vector projection or exclude large orthogonal changes.

DLA-positive-token zero ablation is an informative necessity test despite placing residual activations off distribution and omitting negative-attribution, matched-random, and scale-controlled ablations.
A single fixed temporal-sampling seed is adequate for the reported case study; sampling jitter and ordinary run variation are not characterized.

techniques.role: Compares two clips that share the same action label but differ in the intended success-versus-failure outcome.
Ranks layers and spatiotemporal tokens by contribution to the Bowling class logit.
Projects selected CLS attention maps back onto video frames to inspect ball, pin, and gutter focus.
Tests linear separability of the two clips' CLS activations and exposes the superficial-fingerprint confound.
Uses the strike-minus-gutter activation vector and its layerwise L2 norm as the candidate outcome signal.
Zeros the 313 tokens with highest positive target-logit attribution to test robustness of the Bowling prediction.
Copies strike block activations into the gutter computation to compare causal recovery by architectural component type.
Scores a patch using the norm ratio between patched and original deltas with a dot-product sign correction.

evaluations.setting: One custom 10-second strike clip and one custom 10-second gutter clip, both run through google/vivit-b-16x2-kinetics400 with seed 42
evaluations.metric: Predicted class and layerwise Bowling Direct Logit Attribution
evaluations.result: Both clips are classified as Bowling; target-class confidence grows especially from layer 9 onward
evaluations.baseline: Same pretrained model on the paired clips; no dataset-level or matched-control baseline

evaluations.setting: CLS activations for the same two clips at each of 12 layers
evaluations.baseline: The intended expectation that an abstract outcome distinction would emerge only in later layers; the authors treat the result as a failed fingerprint test

evaluations.result: Approximately 75 at layer 5 and more than 250 at the last layer, reported as more than 300% growth
evaluations.baseline: Earlier-layer delta; no scale-normalized, shuffled-pair, same-outcome, or nuisance-matched distribution
Unablated prediction; no random-token or attribution-sign baseline

evaluations.setting: Strike-to-gutter whole-block activation patching at layers 4-10
evaluations.metric: Signed percentage recovery of the final layer-11 activation delta
evaluations.result: Attention recovers 37.72%-54.41%; MLP recovers 42.10%-60.17%. MLP is higher at layers 4-9, while attention is higher at layer 10 (47.61% versus 43.39%)
evaluations.baseline: Original strike-minus-gutter delta; no confidence intervals, null patches, multi-component sufficiency tests, or alternate recovery metric

limitations: Author-stated: the study uses one strike/gutter video pair and one pretrained VideoViT architecture, so it is a case study rather than a population result.
Author-stated: scene-specific details such as background texture may drive the measured difference; semantic invariance is not established.
Author-stated: manual component-level patching is computationally prohibitive to scale, motivating future automated circuit discovery.
Author-stated: comparisons with standard attribution methods and replications in architectures such as TimeSformer remain future work.

Reviewer-identified: a probe trained on activations from only two underlying videos has no meaningful held-out semantic generalization target; 100% accuracy is expected for arbitrary clip identity differences.

Reviewer-identified: activation-delta L2 magnitude is not evidence that the difference becomes more abstract; residual scale, layer normalization, nuisance accumulation, or unrelated orthogonal features can increase the norm.

Reviewer-identified: preserving the Bowling class after token ablation is a test of the explicit class logit, whereas the proposed hidden outcome is a separate hidden-state observable; robustness of one does not establish independence of the other.
Reviewer-identified: whole attention blocks are patched, not individual heads, so qualitative head labels and causal head-level claims are not supported by the intervention granularity.

Reviewer-identified: the recovery formula uses a norm ratio plus only the sign of a dot product, rather than scalar projection or cosine-aligned recovery; a large mostly orthogonal perturbation can receive a high score.
Reviewer-identified: there are no repeated clips, nuisance-matched pairs, seeds, uncertainty intervals, random-component controls, completeness checks, or held-out validation.
Reviewer-identified: the custom videos and code are available only on request, limiting independent reproduction.

Reviewer-identified: claims about eliciting latent knowledge, hidden cognition, deployment safety, and model knowledge beyond the training task are substantially broader than the evidence from a human-action classifier whose training data can correlate outcomes with visual features.
failure_modes: Changing the lane, camera, bowler, lighting, or trajectory may eliminate or reverse the measured delta if the purported circuit encodes clip identity rather than bowling outcome.
A same-outcome pair with large visual differences may yield an equally large late-layer delta, invalidating the proposed semantic localization criterion.
Zeroing high-attribution tokens can create an off-manifold state and trigger compensation that says little about natural causal necessity.
Distributed positive and negative evidence can survive a top-positive-10% ablation even when the selected regions are behaviorally important.
Block patching may transplant many correlated nuisance features simultaneously, so recovered delta cannot be uniquely assigned to outcome computation.
Nonlinear interactions can make single-block recovery percentages non-additive; partial scores neither prove redundancy nor identify a complete circuit.
The signed norm metric can over-credit orthogonal activation movement or under-credit aligned changes with smaller norm.
Temporal resampling may alter attended frames and recovery rankings despite the one fixed seed.
A different video-transformer architecture, tokenizer, or pretraining dataset may distribute evidence differently and break the attention/MLP pattern.

Outcome features may be encoded without causally influencing the Bowling logit, or the Bowling logit may use outcome-related features without a distinct success/failure variable; the present observables do not distinguish these cases.
reusable_insights: Use same-label contrastive examples to separate within-class latent distinctions from the final class decision, but construct many nuisance-controlled pairs rather than relying on one clip pair.
Treat an unexpectedly perfect early-layer probe as a confound diagnostic: compare against clip identity, background, camera, and shuffled-label controls before calling a feature semantic.
Compare attention and MLP interventions at matched residual-stream locations to test whether routing and feature transformation play different causal roles.
Report both projection onto a hypothesized direction and orthogonal activation change; a single norm-based recovery number obscures their distinction.
Pair sufficiency-style patching with necessity, completeness, and multi-component tests because nonlinear circuits can be redundant and path dependent.
Do not infer independence of an internal representation from a task logit solely because a logit-targeted ablation leaves the class unchanged.
open_questions: Does a classifier trained and tested across many bowlers, lanes, cameras, and paired outcomes recover a scene-invariant strike-versus-gutter direction?
Do same-outcome/different-scene and different-outcome/same-scene controls show that the late-layer norm increase is outcome-specific?
Which individual attention heads, MLP features, and residual paths are necessary and jointly sufficient under a causal-scrubbing or path-patching test?
How do projection-based, cosine, logit-mediated, and behavioral recovery metrics change the attention-versus-MLP ranking?
Does patching the proposed outcome direction change an independent outcome decoder while preserving generic Bowling classification and other scene attributes?
Is the pattern replicated across Kinetics-400 samples, TimeSformer and factorized ViViT variants, preprocessing seeds, and related action classes?
Can automated circuit discovery recover a compact, stable subgraph whose completeness survives held-out interventions?
What evidence threshold would be required before this kind of representation should be called latent knowledge rather than an ordinary within-class visual feature?

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding Video Transformers via Universal Concept Discovery
competitive_landscape.difference: VTCD automatically discovers and ranks high-level spatiotemporal concepts across diverse supervised and self-supervised video transformers and evaluates them on action recognition and video segmentation. The present paper instead performs coarse causal block patching on one same-label outcome pair; its causal intervention is distinctive, but its concept evidence and generality are far narrower.

competitive_landscape.title: Interpretable Action Recognition on Hard to Classify Actions
competitive_landscape.difference: Anichenko et al. build an inherently interpretable action recognizer around explicit objects, hands, depth, and spatiotemporal relations on confusing Something-Something actions. This paper post-hoc analyzes an opaque pretrained ViViT and proposes an internal attention/MLP division of labor, but lacks that work's dataset-level task evaluation and explicit relational representation.

competitive_landscape.title: Paxion: Patching Action Knowledge in Video-Language Foundation Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Paxion introduces ActionBench antonym and video-reversal diagnostics, finds object-recognition shortcuts, and trains a knowledge-patcher module with a discriminative video-dynamics objective, improving action knowledge from roughly 50% to 80%. Here 'patching' means inference-time activation transplantation, not a learned module; the contribution is mechanistic localization in ViViT rather than broad action-knowledge diagnosis or repair.

competitive_landscape.title: Does Circuit Analysis Interpretability Scale? Evidence from Multiple Choice Capabilities in Chinchilla
competitive_landscape.difference: Lieberum et al. combine logit attribution, attention visualization, activation patching, subspace compression, and broader-distribution tests to recover parts of a 70B language-model circuit, explicitly finding that an initially plausible feature explanation is incomplete out of distribution. The present study transfers a subset of those tools to video, but does not perform comparable circuit-completeness or distribution-shift validation.

competitive_landscape.title: ViViT: A Video Vision Transformer
competitive_landscape.difference: ViViT introduces the video-transformer family and joint/factorized space-time attention designs on which the analyzed checkpoint is based. The present paper contributes no new video architecture or action-recognition training result; it is a post-hoc interpretability case study of one pretrained ViViT variant.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: the paper says it reverse-engineers an action-outcome circuit in a pretrained VideoViT, provides causal evidence that attention heads gather evidence while MLPs compose a success concept, and demonstrates hidden knowledge beyond the explicit classification task. Primary prior work already offers automatic video-transformer concept discovery, interpretable relational action recognition, broad action-knowledge diagnostics and repair, and substantially more developed activation-patching circuit analysis. Reviewer inference: the defensible novelty is a compact demonstration of same-label contrastive activation analysis plus attention-versus-MLP whole-block patching in a ViViT bowling case. It is not yet a validated semantic circuit, a head-level mechanism, evidence of task-independent latent knowledge, or a general VideoViT result. Even the claimed uniform MLP dominance must be narrowed to layers 4-9 because Table 3 has higher attention recovery at layer 10.
reviewer_notes: The complete eight-page extraction was read, including methods, all result tables, limitations, broader-impact claims, and references. Quantitative descriptions preserve the distinction between the paper's measured observables and its semantic interpretation. Competing work was independently checked against primary arXiv records. Author claims and reviewer inferences are separated explicitly; the most important internal contradiction is that the prose presents MLP blocks as consistently primary while Table 3 reports layer-10 attention recovery of 47.61%, above the layer-10 MLP's 43.39%.
